name: Resistive voltage divider sensor
summary: Low-power voltage sensor using a resistive divider to give a small voltage signal proportional to primary voltage.
description: A resistive voltage divider sensor is a low-power instrument transformer in which a high-value resistor chain steps the primary voltage down to a small signal. It has no iron core, so it does not cause ferroresonance, and one sensor can cover a wide range of primary voltages.

The output is a low-energy signal that must go to an input designed for it, and the cable between sensor and relay is part of the measurement. The symbol does not show the division ratio, correction factors or connector type, which must match the relay configuration.
readingNotes: Confirm the relay input is configured for the sensor ratio.
Keep the supplied sensor cable unless the manufacturer allows changes.
distinction: A resistive divider sensor gives a low-level signal; a conventional VT gives a standard secondary voltage capable of supplying burden.
